## What the chronicles say [Record]

Anna (Ona), Vytautas's wife, died on 31 July 1418 at Trakai and was buried in Vilnius cathedral (en.wikipedia, Anna, Grand Duchess of Lithuania; pl.wikipedia, Witold Kiejstutowicz; the Lithuanian Wikipedia gives 31 August, a minority date). She is remembered for helping Vytautas escape Krėva in 1382. Her birth year and origins are uncertain. [Vytautas](../characters/vytautas.qmd) married Julijona of Alšėnai, Ona's niece, on 13 November 1418; the Bishop of Vilnius refused for kinship and the Bishop of Włocławek, Jan Kropidło, officiated. Švitrigaila had escaped from Kremenets in March of that year.

## What really happened [Saga]

The book moves her death to the eve of the rye harvest. Her last words show she always knew about the vault and kept it from everyone, as she kept the swap at Krėva. She is the last person who knew Vytautas before the Krėva night. Her last letter, found in a copper-bound box, is read aloud by Julijona at his deathbed: "Grįžk, jei gali. Jei negali, žinok, kad aš žinau."

## Consequences

The graph records no outgoing edge. The saga's consequences are her [husband's second marriage](../characters/julijona.qmd) and, in 1430, her letter at his deathbed.

## Dramatisation

Book IV ch. 9 "Onos Mirtis" (Ona; 31 July 1418, summer), ch. 10 "Julijona" (autumn 1418), and the letter read in ch. 29 "Vilko Mirtis".
